verses.text: Do not boast about tomorrow, because you do not know what a day may bring.
Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth. Let a stranger praise you, not your own lips.
A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but the trouble a fool causes is heavier than both.
Anger is cruel and rage is like a flood, but who can stand up against jealousy?
Open correction is better than hidden love.
The wounds a friend gives can be trusted, but an enemy gives many kisses.
Someone who is full refuses even honey, but to someone who is hungry, even bitter food tastes sweet.
A person who wanders from home is like a bird that wanders from its nest.
Perfume and incense make the heart glad, and so does the sincere advice of a friend.
Do not leave your friend or your father's friend. Do not go to your brother's house when disaster strikes you. A neighbour nearby is better than a brother far away.
Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad. Then I can answer anyone who insults me.
Sensible people see danger coming and hide, but simple people keep going and suffer for it.
Take the coat of someone who guarantees a stranger's debt. Hold it as security if he does it for a woman he does not know.
If you bless your neighbour with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse.
A quarrelling wife is like water dripping on a rainy day.
Trying to control her is like trying to control the wind or hold oil in your hand.
As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.
Whoever takes care of a fig tree will eat its fruit. Whoever looks after their master will be honoured.
As water reflects a face, a person's heart reflects who they really are.
Death and the grave are never satisfied, and people's eyes are never satisfied either.
A melting pot tests silver and a furnace tests gold, and people are tested by the praise they receive.
Even if you crush a fool in a bowl with grain, you will not get his foolishness out of him.
Know well how your flocks are doing. Pay close attention to your herds,
because riches do not last forever, and a crown does not last for all generations.
When the hay is cut and new grass appears, and the grass is gathered from the hills,
your lambs will give you clothes, and your goats will pay for a field.
You will have plenty of goats' milk to feed you, your family, and your servant girls.
